name: National Palace of Sintra
seoTitle: Sintra National Palace: No Bus, No Timed Slot Needed
tagline: The palace in Sintra's town centre: walkable from the station, mostly indoors and the simplest Sintra visit to fit into a port day.

description.short: The royal palace in the centre of Sintra, recognisable by its two conical kitchen chimneys. It is a 10 to 15-minute walk from Sintra station, needs no timed slot and takes about 90 minutes to visit.
description.full:
The National Palace is the Sintra sight with the fewest moving parts. It stands in the town centre, a 10 to 15-minute walk from Sintra station, so there is no bus queue and no hill road. Tickets are for a date, not a time slot, and most of the visit is indoors, which makes it the sensible choice on a wet or misty day, when the views from Pena and the Moorish Castle disappear.

The journey from the Jardim do Tabaco terminal still takes 75 to 90 minutes each way: metro to Restauradores, train from Rossio, then the walk. With about 90 minutes inside, it needs a call of seven to eight hours at the very least.

Choose it over Pena if you care more about interiors than views, if steep hills are a problem, or if your call is at the short end. Choose Pena or Regaleira if you want the image most people associate with Sintra: this palace is plainer outside, and its interest is in the rooms.

The Essential Visit (13 euros) covers the main route. Look for the Swan Room, the largest in the palace; the Magpie Room, with 136 magpies painted on the ceiling; the Room of the Coats of Arms under its heraldic dome; and the kitchen beneath the two chimneys. Hispano-Moresque tiles from the time of Manuel I cover many of the walls. The Full Visit (35 euros) adds Queen Maria Pia's private apartments, seen in a small group at a set time; on a port day it is only worth it if that slot fits your train.

The gardens are free. Quinta da Regaleira is five to ten minutes' walk away, so the two make the most practical pair in Sintra on a long call. The ticket office closes from 12:00 to 13:00, so buy online or use the machines. The Swan Room is occasionally restricted for events; the Parques de Sintra notices page lists these.
description.history: The palace probably began as the residence of Sintra's Moorish governors; the 10th-century geographer Al-Bakri already mentions Sintra and its castle. After 1147 the site passed to the Portuguese crown, and the first document recording a palace here dates from 1281, under King Dinis. João I (reigned 1385-1433) rebuilt it around a central patio, adding the Swan Room and the kitchen with its two chimneys. Manuel I added the Room of the Coats of Arms and much of the tilework in the early 16th century. Afonso VI was held prisoner here from 1674 until his death nine years later. Queen Maria Pia was the last royal resident, leaving for exile in 1910.
description.significance: Parques de Sintra describes it as the only palace that spans the whole history of Portugal: almost every monarch lived here at some point, from the Middle Ages to 1910. The Room of the Coats of Arms, displaying the arms of 72 noble families, is one of the most important heraldic rooms in Europe. For a visitor, it shows royal life before the Romantic era that produced Pena and Monserrate.

directions.general: Located in the historic center of Sintra village, the palace is easily identifiable by its two massive conical chimneys
directions.fromCruisePort: Walk about 10 minutes to Santa Apolónia and take the metro Blue Line to Restauradores; Rossio station is a two-minute walk. Trains from Rossio reach Sintra in about 40 minutes. From Sintra station walk 10 to 15 minutes to the palace in Largo Rainha D. Amélia, or take Scotturb bus 434 or 435. Allow 75 to 90 minutes door to door each way.
directions.publicTransport: CP train from Lisbon (Rossio, Oriente or Entrecampos) to Sintra on the Sintra line. From Sintra station, walk 10 to 15 minutes or take Scotturb bus 434 or 435.
directions.parking: Private cars are restricted to residents in the historic centre. Use the car parks outside it and walk or take the bus.

openingTimes.currentStatus: Open daily except 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January

seasonal.notes: Ticket office closed 12:00-13:00; ticket machines available

admissionPrices.notes: Essential Visit (palace route and gardens): adults 18-64 13 euros, youths 6-17 and seniors 65+ 10 euros, children under 6 free, family (2 adults + 2 youths) 35 euros. Full Visit, adding Queen Maria Pia's apartments in a small group at a set time: adults 35 euros, youths 20 euros, seniors 25 euros, family 95 euros. Guided visit: adults 45 euros. Gardens free. Tickets are for a specific date; online tickets can be rescheduled until 18:00 the day before.

visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Opening time or after 15:00. Weekdays are quieter than weekends. A good choice on rainy or misty days.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Buy a date ticket online before you sail. The ticket office closes from 12:00 to 13:00. Last entry 17:30. The gardens are free. Pair with Quinta da Regaleira, five to ten minutes' walk away, on a long call.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 4.5 hours door to door (75-90 minutes each way plus about 90 minutes inside); needs a call of 7-8 hours or more
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Metro, a 40-minute train and a 10-15 minute uphill walk on cobbles (or bus 434/435). Inside, the route has stairs between levels and some uneven floors.
tips: Tickets are for a date, not a time slot: buy the Essential Visit (13 euros) online before you sail and arrive whenever your train does.
Walk from Sintra station (10 to 15 minutes) rather than queueing for bus 434 or 435 in summer.
The ticket office closes from 12:00 to 13:00; the ticket machines keep working.
Last entry to the palace is 17:30; the gardens stay open until 18:30 and are free.
The Full Visit (35 euros) adds Queen Maria Pia's apartments with a small group at a set time; skip it unless the slot fits your return train.
On a wet or misty day this is the Sintra sight that loses least, because Pena and the Moorish Castle are mostly about views.
Pair it with Quinta da Regaleira, five to ten minutes' walk away, only on calls of about ten hours or more.
Closed 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January; the Swan Room is sometimes restricted for events, so check the official notices.

highlights: Two conical kitchen chimneys, the landmark of Sintra's skyline
Swan Room, the largest room, with swans painted on the ceiling
Magpie Room, with 136 magpies holding João I's motto 'por bem'
Room of the Coats of Arms, with the arms of Manuel I, his children and 72 noble families on its dome
Hispano-Moresque tilework from the reign of Manuel I
Central Patio, the core of João I's palace
Queen Maria Pia's apartments (Full Visit only)
Preta Garden, restored and free to visit
facilities: Free Zoomguide digital audio guide (Portuguese, English, Spanish, French)

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Ground floor and some rooms are accessible. Upper floors require stairs. Historic building with some narrow passages and uneven floors. Gardens are more accessible than interior
